title: Accounting Note: Credits Deducted from Employer Benefit Charging Protest Relief
content:
Accounting note for Employer Benefit Charging. When a protest is granted, credits that already stand on the position may be deducted from what the protest relief reaches.

**Rule.** Where a credit for a recovered overpayment stands on the position, every credit already posted on the position is deducted; where credits for cancelled payments stand on it but none for a recovered overpayment, those cancelled-payment credits are deducted; where no credit stands on it, nothing is deducted.

The credits looked at are all credits posted on the position, in every quarter, identified by the credit reason each carries.

| Credits standing on the position | Deducted |
|---|---|
| At least one recovered-overpayment credit | Every credit already posted on the position, of whatever reason |
| Cancelled-payment credits, no recovered-overpayment credit | The cancelled-payment credits only |
| Neither a recovered-overpayment nor a cancelled-payment credit | Nothing |

The last row includes a position with no credit at all, and a position whose only credits carry another reason, such as a relief or an appeal reversal.

**Examples (hypothetical ledgers).**

| Credits on the position | Deducted |
|---|---|
| Recovered overpayment $60.00; cancelled payment $95.00; relief $20.00 | $175.00 |
| Cancelled payment $95.00; cancelled payment $40.00 | $135.00 |
| Appeal reversal $70.00 | Nothing |
| None | Nothing |
